children: Latvia's state-backed national carrier, airBaltic, filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday to restructure its debt and downsize its fleet.

Under the proposed restructuring, the company aims to convert a portion of its senior secured bonds into equity while downsizing its fleet from 54 to roughly 36 aircraft by late 2026, according to court papers filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Manhattan. The airline said it would maintain normal operations during the bankruptcy.

AirBaltic had struggled to overcome the lasting impact of the Covid-19 pandemic, which caused roughly EUR455 million ($527.8 million) in losses from 2020 to 2022. Since then, heavy debt loads and geopolitical headwinds from Russia's war in Ukraine, as well as the sharp doubling of jet fuel prices caused by the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, have weighed on earnings.
The airline was also hit by severe engine shortages for its Airbus A220 aircraft, forcing it to pay for idle planes while hiring substitute aircraft.

AirBaltic attempted to negotiate an out-of-court deal with holders of its EUR398.2 million senior secured bonds maturing in 2029. However, after facing extreme financial pressure, the company secured a EUR350 million debtor-in-possession loan from a third-party lender group led by Strategic Value Partners, according to the filing.

The airline, which is 88% owned by the Latvian government, plans to use the court process to address its lease obligations. It plans to return about 20 surplus aircraft to lessors and renegotiate its current lease rates.

Founded in 1995, airBaltic is the major carrier in the Baltic region, operating out of its primary hub in Riga, Latvia, along with secondary bases in Tallinn, Estonia; Vilnius, Lithuania; and Gran Canaria, Spain. The company transported more than 5.2 million passengers in 2025, according to court documents. Deutsche Lufthansa owns a 10% stake in the company.

Milbank and Cobalt Latvia are acting as legal counsel and Seabury Global Aviation Advisors is serving as financial adviser and investment banker. The case, No. 26-12188, has been assigned to Judge Lisa Beckerman.
